facts.name: Program audience and curriculum focus
facts.detail: Program page: the M.S. is tailored to working professionals and is described as offering a current computing curriculum.
facts.quote: Tailored to the schedules of working professionals, the CSULB Master of Science in Computer Science program offers the most relevant and up-to-date curriculum to meet the demands of the rapidly changing world of computing.

facts.name: Advanced study areas
facts.detail: Program page: the M.S. provides advanced study in software development and engineering, networking, operating systems, distributed computing, AI, and algorithm analysis.
facts.quote: The M.S. in Computer Science provides advanced study in software development and engineering, networking, operating systems, distributed computing, artificial intelligence, and analysis of algorithms.

facts.name: Concentrations
facts.detail: Students can pursue concentrations in Advanced Systems or Software Development.
facts.quote: Students can pursue concentrations in Advanced Systems or Software Development.

facts.name: Culminating experience
facts.detail: Students finish with a comprehensive exam or a thesis research project.
facts.quote: Complete your graduate degree with a comprehensive exam or thesis research project.

facts.name: Bachelor's degree and GPA
facts.detail: MSCS admissions: bachelor's in computer engineering or computer science, or sufficient background, with a minimum 2.7 GPA in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units.
facts.quote: Hold a bachelor's degree in computer engineering or computer science or have sufficient background in computer engineering or computer science from a college or university with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units attempted.

facts.name: University graduate admission requirements
facts.detail: The MSCS admissions page also requires applicants to satisfy university requirements for graduate admission.
facts.quote: Satisfy university requirements for graduate admission

facts.name: University minimum GPA options (university-wide)
facts.detail: University-wide graduate standing page: a baccalaureate with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5, with no rounding. This is a university rule, not an MSCS-only rule.
facts.quote: Hold a baccalaureate degree with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5. (No Rounding)

facts.name: Catalog heading
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 University Catalog program heading is Computer Science, M.S.
facts.quote: Computer Science, M.S.

facts.name: Program mission
facts.detail: The catalog describes a graduate program meant to prepare leaders in industry and also students who later pursue advanced degrees, with advanced courses in software and hardware analysis and design.
facts.quote: The mission of the graduate program in Computer Science at CSULB is to provide a high-quality educational experience and the technical specialization required to become successful leaders in industry.

facts.name: Thesis or comprehensive examination
facts.detail: Students may finish with a thesis or a comprehensive examination.
facts.quote: The students may choose to do a thesis or take a comprehensive examination as the culmination of their program.

facts.name: Admission degree background
facts.detail: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in computer engineering or computer science, or sufficient background in those fields, from a college or university.
facts.quote: To be considered for admission the graduate applicant must have earned a bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science or sufficient background in computer engineering or computer science from a college or university

facts.name: Admission GPA of 2.7 in last 60 semester units
facts.detail: The minimum GPA is 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units attempted.
facts.quote: a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper division major units attempted.

facts.name: Apply through Cal State Apply, not the department
facts.detail: Applications go through Cal State Apply; the page says not to send an application to the department. International students also apply at Cal State Apply.
facts.quote: The student should apply online at www.calstate.edu/apply . Do not send an application to the Department.

facts.name: Remove deficiencies before graduate-level courses
facts.detail: All deficiencies must be removed before a student attempts graduate-level courses.
facts.quote: All deficiencies must be removed before attempting graduate-level courses.

facts.name: Advancement to candidacy: deficiencies and overall GPA
facts.detail: Students applying for advancement to candidacy must have completed all undergraduate deficiencies with grades of C or better and have an overall GPA of 3.0.
facts.quote: Students applying for advancement to candidacy must: have completed all undergraduate deficiencies with grades of "C" or better; have attained an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.0;

facts.name: Advancement to candidacy: 9 units and advisor approval
facts.detail: They must also complete at least 9 units of required degree-applicable courses with a 3.0 GPA in those units, and have a plan of study approved by the CECS department graduate advisor.
facts.quote: have completed at least 9 units of required courses applicable to the degree with a GPA of at least 3.0 for the completed units; and have their plans of studies approved by the CECS department graduate advisor.

facts.name: Degree unit total
facts.detail: The degree requires 30 units.
facts.quote: Degree Requirements (30 units)

facts.name: First-semester plan of study
facts.detail: Students must meet the Graduate Program Adviser at the start of the first semester to make a tentative plan of study. The page also says a detailed required-and-elective list is kept on the Graduate Program website.
facts.quote: Students must meet with the Graduate Program Adviser at the beginning of their first semester to create a tentative plan of study.

facts.name: Culminating options and 400-level cap
facts.detail: Students must choose the Thesis Option or the Comprehensive Exam Option. At most 9 units of 400-level coursework may count toward the degree.
facts.quote: As a culminating activity, students must elect either the Thesis Option or the Comprehensive Exam Option. A maximum of 9 units of 400-level coursework may be applied toward the degree.

facts.name: Comprehensive exam option unit split
facts.detail: The exam option requires 30 graduate hours in computer science, a passing comprehensive exam, 15 units of required core courses, and 15 units of allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: Student must complete 30 graduate hours credit in computer science and pass the comprehensive exam. 15 units of required core courses

facts.name: Exam-option elective units
facts.detail: Under the comprehensive exam option, students take 15 units from the allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: 15 units from allowed electives (No more than 9 units may be from the 400 level courses.)

facts.name: Comprehensive exam covered courses
facts.detail: The comprehensive exam covers CECS 524, CECS 528, and CECS 543. The page does not list CECS 530 or CECS 558 among the covered courses, even though those two are in the required core.
facts.quote: Comprehensive examination covering the following required courses: CECS 524 - Advanced Topics in Programming Languages (3 units) CECS 528 - Advanced Analysis of Algorithms (3 units) CECS 543 - Advanced Software Engineering (3 units)

facts.name: Thesis option unit split
facts.detail: The thesis option requires 15 units of required courses, 9 units of allowed electives (no more than 9 units from 400-level courses), and 6 units of research and thesis.
facts.quote: 15 units of required courses

facts.name: Thesis-option elective units
facts.detail: Under the thesis option, students take 9 units from allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: 9 units from allowed electives (No more than 9 units may be from the 400 level courses.);

facts.name: Thesis research and report
facts.detail: The thesis option includes 6 units of research and thesis with a written report and oral presentation approved by the thesis committee. At least 3 of those units must be CECS 698; the remaining 3 units may be CECS 697 or CECS 698.
facts.quote: 6 units of research and thesis with written report and oral presentation approved by the thesis committee.

facts.name: Thesis minimum from CECS 698
facts.detail: At least 3 of the 6 thesis-option research units must be taken from CECS 698 Thesis or Industrial Project.
facts.quote: At least 3 units must be taken from the following course CECS 698 - Thesis or Industrial Project (3-6 units)

facts.name: Thesis remaining 3 units
facts.detail: The remaining 3 thesis research units may be CECS 697 Directed Research or CECS 698 Thesis or Industrial Project.
facts.quote: Remaining 3 units may be taken from either of the following courses CECS 697 - Directed Research (1-3 units) CECS 698 - Thesis or Industrial Project (3-6 units)

facts.name: CECS 524
facts.detail: CECS 524 Advanced Topics in Programming Languages, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Intensive study of languages of current interest which support object-oriented, client-server, and multimedia applications (e.g. JAVA). Master's students register in CECS 524 or CECS 624 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 624 .
facts.quote: Intensive study of languages of current interest which support object-oriented, client-server, and multimedia applications (e.g. JAVA). Master's students register in CECS 524 or CECS 624 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 624 .

facts.name: CECS 528
facts.detail: CECS 528 Advanced Analysis of Algorithms, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Theoretical analysis of algorithms. Divide and conquer, dynamic programming and greedy algorithms; basic search and traversal techniques including search trees; sorting; matrix manipulations; NP-completeness. Master's students register in CECS 528 or CECS 628 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 628 .
facts.quote: Theoretical analysis of algorithms. Divide and conquer, dynamic programming and greedy algorithms; basic search and traversal techniques including search trees; sorting; matrix manipulations; NP-completeness. Master's students register in CECS 528 or CECS 628 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 628 .

facts.name: CECS 530
facts.detail: CECS 530 Advanced Computer Architecture I, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Fundamentals of computer architecture. Parallelism, Instruction Level Parallelism, Pipelining. Hazards and their management, Branch Prediction, Dynamic Scheduling, Multiple Instructions, Multithreading, Data Level Parallelism, SIMD, Graphic Processing Units, Memory Hierarchy, Cache, Virtual Memory
facts.quote: Fundamentals of computer architecture. Parallelism, Instruction Level Parallelism, Pipelining. Hazards and their management, Branch Prediction, Dynamic Scheduling, Multiple Instructions, Multithreading, Data Level Parallelism, SIMD, Graphic Processing Units, Memory Hierarchy, Cache, Virtual Memory

facts.name: CECS 543
facts.detail: CECS 543 Advanced Software Engineering, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Study of software engineering as a broad, problem-solving discipline. Includes structured programming and software project management. Master's students register in CECS 543 or CECS 643 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 643 . Additional projects required for CECS 643 .
facts.quote: Study of software engineering as a broad, problem-solving discipline. Includes structured programming and software project management. Master's students register in CECS 543 or CECS 643 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 643 . Additional projects required for CECS 643 .

facts.name: CECS 558
facts.detail: CECS 558 Deep Learning, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Foundational and advanced deep learning concepts. Introduction to neural networks, backpropagation, specialized neural network architectures, deep reinforcement learning, and large language models. Programming assignments to reinforce understanding.
facts.quote: Foundational and advanced deep learning concepts. Introduction to neural networks, backpropagation, specialized neural network architectures, deep reinforcement learning, and large language models. Programming assignments to reinforce understanding.

facts.name: CECS 698
facts.detail: CECS 698 Thesis or Industrial Project, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Computer Engineering MS, Computer Science MS, and Engineering MS students only. Planning, preparation, completion of thesis or equivalent industrial project report on a suitable topic in computer engineering and computer science following the library's prescribed format.
facts.quote: Computer Engineering MS, Computer Science MS, and Engineering MS students only. Planning, preparation, completion of thesis or equivalent industrial project report on a suitable topic in computer engineering and computer science following the library's prescribed format.

facts.name: CECS 697
facts.detail: CECS 697 Directed Research, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Theoretical and experimental problems in computer science and engineering requiring extensive research. Advancement to candidacy and program GPA of at least 3.0 are required. Graduate advisor and project supervisor must be consulted prior to registration. Independent Study.
facts.quote: Theoretical and experimental problems in computer science and engineering requiring extensive research. Advancement to candidacy and program GPA of at least 3.0 are required. Graduate advisor and project supervisor must be consulted prior to registration. Independent Study.

facts.name: CECS 519
facts.detail: CECS 519 Theory of Computation, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Advanced topics in computability theory and computational complexity theory. Topics include Turing Machines, coverage of the standard complexity classes P, NP, IP, and PSPACE, hierarchy, decidability, and recognizability theorems. Additional projects required for CECS 519.
facts.quote: Advanced topics in computability theory and computational complexity theory. Topics include Turing Machines, coverage of the standard complexity classes P, NP, IP, and PSPACE, hierarchy, decidability, and recognizability theorems. Additional projects required for CECS 519.

facts.name: CECS 521
facts.detail: CECS 521 Database Architecture, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Relational database design theory-a rigorous approach. Security, recovery, transaction management, distributed databases and query optimization. Master's students register in CECS 521 or CECS 621 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 621 . Additional projects required for CECS 621 .
facts.quote: Relational database design theory-a rigorous approach. Security, recovery, transaction management, distributed databases and query optimization. Master's students register in CECS 521 or CECS 621 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 621 . Additional projects required for CECS 621 .

facts.name: CECS 526
facts.detail: CECS 526 Advanced Operating Systems, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Theoretical foundations of concepts applied in the design of operating systems. Control of concurrent processes, deadlocks, mutual exclusion, virtual memory, resource management and scheduling. Master's students register in CECS 526 or CECS 626 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 626 .
facts.quote: Theoretical foundations of concepts applied in the design of operating systems. Control of concurrent processes, deadlocks, mutual exclusion, virtual memory, resource management and scheduling. Master's students register in CECS 526 or CECS 626 ; Ph.D. students register in CECS 626 .

facts.name: CECS 529
facts.detail: CECS 529 Search Engine Technology, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Models, algorithms, and evaluation of the retrieval of information from a collection of documents. Document preprocessing. Indexing and searching. Retrieval evaluation. Search engines. Additional projects required for CECS 529.
facts.quote: Models, algorithms, and evaluation of the retrieval of information from a collection of documents. Document preprocessing. Indexing and searching. Retrieval evaluation. Search engines. Additional projects required for CECS 529.

facts.name: CECS 532
facts.detail: CECS 532 Memory Design and Implementation, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Logic design and operation, physical design and operation, performance characteristics, design trade-offs, energy consumption of modern memory hierarchies, memory errors and error correction.
facts.quote: Logic design and operation, physical design and operation, performance characteristics, design trade-offs, energy consumption of modern memory hierarchies, memory errors and error correction.

facts.name: CECS 544
facts.detail: CECS 544 Software Testing and Verification, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Testing/verification techniques for software development including black box, white box, incremental, top-down and bottom-up, static and dynamic, performance, regression, thread, and stress testing. Object-oriented software testing with a hierarchical approach.
facts.quote: Testing/verification techniques for software development including black box, white box, incremental, top-down and bottom-up, static and dynamic, performance, regression, thread, and stress testing. Object-oriented software testing with a hierarchical approach.

facts.name: CECS 545
facts.detail: CECS 545 Software Architecture, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Includes architectural styles, pipes and filters, data abstraction and object-oriented organization, event-based, implicit invocation, layered systems, repositories, interpreters, process control, distributed processes, domain-specific software & heterogeneous architectures.
facts.quote: Includes architectural styles, pipes and filters, data abstraction and object-oriented organization, event-based, implicit invocation, layered systems, repositories, interpreters, process control, distributed processes, domain-specific software & heterogeneous architectures.

facts.name: CECS 546
facts.detail: CECS 546 Fault Tolerant Computing Systems, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Fault tolerant techniques are studied as tools to assure the reliability and continuous availability of computing systems. Case studies of modern fault tolerant systems reviewed.
facts.quote: Fault tolerant techniques are studied as tools to assure the reliability and continuous availability of computing systems. Case studies of modern fault tolerant systems reviewed.

facts.name: CECS 547
facts.detail: CECS 547 Software Maintenance, Reengineering and Reuse, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Introduction to software maintenance, defect management, corrective, adaptive and perfective maintenance. Evolution of legacy software systems. Program comprehension techniques, reverse engineering, restructuring, refactoring of software systems. Software re-engineering, data reverse engineering.
facts.quote: Introduction to software maintenance, defect management, corrective, adaptive and perfective maintenance. Evolution of legacy software systems. Program comprehension techniques, reverse engineering, restructuring, refactoring of software systems. Software re-engineering, data reverse engineering.

facts.name: CECS 550
facts.detail: CECS 550 Pattern Recognition, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: General concepts of pattern recognition and trainable classifiers, decision theory, supervised learning, non-parametric techniques, rule-based systems and neural networks. Master's students register in CECS 550; Ph.D. students register in CECS 650 . Additional projects required for CECS 650 .
facts.quote: General concepts of pattern recognition and trainable classifiers, decision theory, supervised learning, non-parametric techniques, rule-based systems and neural networks. Master's students register in CECS 550; Ph.D. students register in CECS 650 . Additional projects required for CECS 650 .

facts.name: CECS 551
facts.detail: CECS 551 Advanced Artificial Intelligence, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Advanced concepts in artificial intelligence. Topics include knowledge acquisition and representation, fuzzy logic, logical reasoning, multi-sensor integration, Dempster-Shafer's theory of evidential reasoning, real-time expert systems and neural networks.
facts.quote: Advanced concepts in artificial intelligence. Topics include knowledge acquisition and representation, fuzzy logic, logical reasoning, multi-sensor integration, Dempster-Shafer's theory of evidential reasoning, real-time expert systems and neural networks.

facts.name: CECS 552
facts.detail: CECS 552 Computer Simulation and Modeling, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Studies of general purpose and special simulation software. Model verification including graphical models Applications in various areas. Master's students register in CECS 552
facts.quote: Studies of general purpose and special simulation software. Model verification including graphical models Applications in various areas. Master's students register in CECS 552

facts.name: CECS 553
facts.detail: CECS 553 Machine Vision, CSULB 2026-27 catalog: Discussion and laboratory implementation of current research in vision and image understanding. Topics include image formation, early processing, segmentation, relational structures in 2-D and 3-D, motion, stereo, 3-D reconstruction, morphological methods and computer architecture for machine
facts.quote: Discussion and laboratory implementation of current research in vision and image understanding. Topics include image formation, early processing, segmentation, relational structures in 2-D and 3-D, motion, stereo, 3-D reconstruction, morphological methods and computer architecture for machine

facts.name: CECS 561
